recipes.title: Sunday Spaghetti
recipes.subtitle: A little garlic. A slow simmer. A very good dinner.
recipes.source: Oui Chef development recipe. Kitchen review pending.

instructions.cook_pasta: Add spaghetti to the boiling water and stir. The 8-minute reminder is a starting point; use the package time and check the texture. Start when the pasta is in the water.

alternatives.name: Rice spaghetti
alternatives.note: Use the same dry weight. Check the package ingredients and cross-contact information; follow its cooking time.

instructions.cook_pasta: Add the rice spaghetti to boiling water and stir gently. Follow its package cooking time and taste for tenderness; the reminder is only a check-in. Start when the pasta is in the water.

ratios.title: Sauce to pasta
ratios.explanation: Keep the pasta amount fixed; adjust tomatoes before starting the sauce.

ratios.title: Sauce seasoning
ratios.explanation: Adjust only the sauce salt before cooking; pasta water seasoning stays separate.

nodes.title: Prepare the garlic
nodes.instruction: Peel and finely chop the garlic. Measure the other ingredients.

nodes.title: Bring water to a boil
nodes.instruction: Add the measured water and pasta-water salt to a large pot. Bring to a boil.
nodes.criterion: Is the water at a rolling boil?

nodes.title: Soften the garlic
nodes.instruction: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and stir until fragrant and lightly golden.
nodes.criterion: Is the garlic fragrant and lightly golden, without dark edges?

coachingCues.text: How is the garlic looking? We want lightly golden edges; lower the heat if it is darkening quickly.

nodes.title: Simmer the sauce
nodes.instruction: Add the tomatoes and sauce salt to the garlic oil. Bring to a gentle simmer and stir occasionally. Start when the sauce is simmering.
nodes.criterion: Has the sauce thickened enough to coat a spoon?

coachingCues.text: How is the sauce coming along? It should be gently bubbling. Give it a stir and check whether it is starting to thicken.

nodes.title: Cook the spaghetti
nodes.instruction: Add spaghetti to the boiling water and stir. The 8-minute reminder is a starting point; use the package time and check the texture. Start when the pasta is in the water.
nodes.criterion: Have you tasted a cooled piece? It should be tender with the bite you like.

coachingCues.text: We are getting close. Check your pasta packet, and let me know when a cooled piece has the bite you like.

nodes.title: Bring it all together
nodes.instruction: Reserve a little pasta water, drain the spaghetti, and toss it with the sauce. Add reserved water a spoonful at a time if needed.
nodes.criterion: Does the sauce coat the pasta evenly?

nodes.title: Dinner is ready
nodes.instruction: Divide the spaghetti between your bowls and serve.
nodes.criterion: Is everything plated and ready to enjoy?

recoveryOptions.title: Add unsalted tomatoes
recoveryOptions.instruction: Use unsalted tomatoes of the same checked product. Stir the measured extra tomatoes into the sauce and simmer until combined. This dilutes seasoning but may change acidity; taste before adding more.
recoveryOptions.criterion: Has the sauce combined, and is the seasoning more comfortable?

recipes.title: Your First Loaf
recipes.subtitle: Flour-dusted hands. A golden crust. You made this.
recipes.source: Development adaptation; method reference: https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/recipes/hearth-bread-recipe . Kitchen review pending.

ratios.title: Water to flour
ratios.explanation: Flour stays fixed. More water makes a softer, stickier dough; use the texture checks rather than adding extra flour automatically.

nodes.title: Mix the dough
nodes.instruction: Combine flour, yeast, salt, sugar, and lukewarm water until no dry pockets remain.
nodes.criterion: Have all the ingredients come together?

nodes.title: Knead the dough
nodes.instruction: Knead on a clean surface until smooth and elastic. Use a light dusting of flour only if needed.
nodes.criterion: Does the dough feel smooth and stretchy?

coachingCues.text: How does the dough feel now? Look for a smoother surface and more stretch.

nodes.title: First rise
nodes.instruction: Cover the dough in its bowl and leave in a comfortably warm place. Start this timer once it is resting.
nodes.criterion: Has the dough grown to roughly twice its original volume?

coachingCues.text: This is the first rise. How is the volume looking? We are checking growth, not just the clock.

nodes.title: Shape the loaf
nodes.instruction: Gently release large air pockets, form a loaf, and place on a lined baking tray. Cover loosely.
nodes.criterion: Is the shaped loaf covered on the tray?

nodes.title: Second rise
nodes.instruction: Let the shaped dough rise again until noticeably puffy. Start when the covered loaf is resting.
nodes.criterion: Is the shaped loaf noticeably puffier than when you started?

coachingCues.text: We are on the second rise now. How is your shaped loaf looking—has it become noticeably puffy?

nodes.title: Preheat the oven
nodes.instruction: Set the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Keep the rising dough outside the oven.

nodes.title: Bake the loaf
nodes.instruction: Uncover the loaf and carefully place its tray in the heated oven. Start the timer after it goes in.
nodes.criterion: Is the loaf deeply golden, with a firm crust? Check the center is baked through before cooling.

coachingCues.text: How is the crust coloring? Check through the oven window if you can; we are looking for a golden crust.

nodes.title: Cool the bread
nodes.instruction: Using oven mitts, move the loaf to a rack. Let it cool before slicing.
nodes.criterion: Has the loaf cooled enough to slice without a gummy center?

recoveryOptions.title: Moisten dry dough
recoveryOptions.instruction: Work the measured extra water into the dough gradually, then knead until evenly absorbed. Pause to feel its texture before considering another addition.
recoveryOptions.criterion: Is the dough hydrated and smooth rather than dry or tearing?

recipes.title: The Classic Margarita
recipes.subtitle: Bright lime, good tequila, and a moment to unwind.
recipes.source: Ratio reference: https://iba-world.com/iba-cocktail/margarita/ . Original guidance; kitchen review pending.

ratios.title: Liqueur to tequila
ratios.explanation: Keep tequila fixed; adjust liqueur before mixing. This changes flavor balance and total volume.

ratios.title: Lime to tequila
ratios.explanation: Keep tequila fixed; adjust the lime for a brighter or softer balance.

nodes.title: Measure your ingredients
nodes.instruction: Measure the tequila, orange liqueur, and fresh lime juice using the quantities above.
nodes.criterion: Are the measured ingredients ready to combine?

nodes.title: Shake with ice
nodes.instruction: Add the measured ingredients and ice to the shaker. Seal firmly and shake. For two drinks, split into batches if your shaker is crowded.
nodes.criterion: Does the shaker feel thoroughly cold?

coachingCues.text: Keep the shaker firmly closed. Let me know when it feels nice and cold.

nodes.title: Pour and enjoy
nodes.instruction: Strain into your serving glass, leaving the ice in the shaker.
nodes.criterion: Is your drink strained and ready?

recoveryOptions.title: Restore the original balance
recoveryOptions.instruction: Check the extra ingredients, then add the measured additions. Split into batches if needed, shake again with ice, and taste before serving. The larger batch contains more alcohol; share it as additional servings.
recoveryOptions.criterion: Is the drink balanced to your taste, and thoroughly chilled?
